newsitem.title: UK: Zinc slow in Europe physical market, lead slumbers.
newsitem.headline: Zinc slow in Europe physical market, lead slumbers.

text.p: Spot physical markets in lead and zinc in Europe have been slow this week, partly because of high prices, particularly in the latter metal, traders said.
The zinc market reached a 4-1/2 year high on the London Metal Exchange (LME) of $1,256 a tonne on Tuesday, but has since settled some $20 lower.
"Frame contracts are going on all the time and people are pricing tonnage through, but on the spot side they are holding back," one trader said.
Zinc's price rise has been driven by strong demand from the U.S., falling stocks, and, most recently, an influx of investment fund interest.
Because the speculative flow has pushed prices higher in a short period of time, those consumers who need to take material off the spot market are holding back, hoping for a downside reaction.
However, there has been reasonable enquiry for second-half 1997 requirements, although very little business is being booked, they noted.
In lead, the physical sector remains slow, and with the LME backwardation and April tightness slackening premiums are not moving.
The tightness is seen as a short-term technical operation by a major merchant, which may flare up again but will not be representative of underlying fundamentals.
"There is no shortage of lead - in fact, it may well be in oversupply by the end of the year," a trader said.
Similar slow conditions prevailed in other physical markets, and there was equally little change in the premium structures.
"In a lot of these markets, prices have moved up to high levels, and the real users will take time to get used to that," an aluminium trader said.
Nearby physicals in aluminium remain underpinned by strong U.S. levels, although the high premiums there may start to ease when LME metal arrives.
Spot trades have been as high as six cents/lb, but indications for the second half are nearer a more comfortable 4.5 cents, traders noted.
In copper, the spot market continues to be affected by high cash prices, although the cash/March contango has seen some offers for LME warrants in Italy around the $10/12 level.
"Consumers are underbought, but the high cash price is restraining them," a copper trader said.
